answer.rationale:
Constraints prune most of the option space before evidence matters. Rollback is off the table: compliance has ruled the security patch non-revertible, so memory_b1 is irrelevant here regardless of how strong that record is — no point spending the single verification on it. Regional failover (memory_b2) addressed a latency degradation whose cause was regional; nothing here suggests a region-specific fault, and shifting traffic mid-peak with heavy in-flight writes risks exactly the customer-write loss the objective forbids. Adding capacity (memory_b3) worked when provisioned ahead of a known peak; we are already inside the peak with a 90-minute climb, and new capacity rarely lands fast enough to bend a curve already at 5x. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) contained an external partner failure by failing fast — but failing fast on our own write path means dropping settlement writes, which directly violates the primary objective.

That leaves read-replica routing as the only lever that plausibly relieves the primary without shedding writes or touching the patched build. It is also the lever I am leaning on hardest, so it is where verification buys the most: memory_b5 is a single episode, and I want the original record to check whether the load it moved was actually contending with the write path, how long recovery took, and whether the primary's bottleneck then resembles ours now. If the archived record shows the relief came from a different contention mechanism, my reasoning collapses and I would rather learn that before committing.

Important caveat: the causal story is unconfirmed. The latency climb began roughly around the release window, and I cannot yet rule out the new build as the driver — in which case read offload treats a symptom and buys time at best. Because the patch cannot be reverted, buying time is still worth something.

Downstream value risk: routing reads to replicas introduces replica lag into whatever consumes those queries. If settlement reconciliation, balance displays, or compliance reporting read through this path, they will silently serve stale financial data during peak — a correctness harm that looks like success on a latency dashboard. So: scope the cutover to report/dashboard queries only, exclude anything on the settlement or reconciliation read path, verify lag bounds before widening, and hold a rollback of the routing change itself. Instrument write p99 and replica lag together so a false recovery signal is visible.
